domain.label: Context & Setup
domain.description: Anchors for interpretation and personalization (not scored as symptoms).

questions.text: Child's age (in years)?
Child's grade / program (e.g., preschool, K, 2nd grade, SPED classroom, homeschool)?
Primary language spoken at home (or most used language)?
Does your child currently receive ABA therapy?
Does your child currently receive speech therapy?
Does your child currently receive occupational therapy (OT)?
Does your child have an IEP/504 or receive school-based services?
Which description best matches your child's CURRENT spoken communication level?
Which description best matches your child's CURRENT understanding of spoken language?

options.label: Often seems not to understand spoken language
Understands simple instructions but misses nuance

questions.text: Top 3 goals for the next 3 months (free text).

domain.label: Safety & Red Flags
domain.description: Identify urgent risks that may require immediate planning or clinical follow-up.

questions.text: Has your child run off / eloped (bolted away from supervision) in the last 3 months?
Has your child shown unsafe bolting into streets/parking lots in the last 3 months?
Has your child left home or a safe area unsupervised (even briefly) in the last 3 months?
In the last month, has your child been aggressive in a way that could cause injury (hitting, biting, kicking, throwing objects)?
In the last month, has your child injured themself (head banging, biting self, scratching) leaving marks/bruises?
Any possible skill regression in the last 6 months (loss of language, toileting, social interest, daily skills)?
Any seizures or episodes of staring/unresponsiveness that concern you?
Significant feeding/weight/hydration concern (not gaining weight, significant loss, dehydration risk)?
Severe sleep deprivation most nights (very little sleep or frequent long night wakings) impacting daytime function?

domain.label: Social Communication
domain.description: Social attention, reciprocity, shared enjoyment, and peer engagement.

questions.text: Responds to name when not fully absorbed in an activity.
Makes eye contact to connect (not only to request items/help).
Shares enjoyment (shows/points to interesting things, invites you to look).
Seeks others out just to be with them (not only for items/needs).
Back-and-forth interaction (2+ turns) during play or conversation.
Uses gestures naturally (pointing, nodding, waving, shrugging).
Understands and uses turn-taking in games/interaction.
Notices others’ feelings and responds (comforts, asks, adjusts behavior).
Plays with peers cooperatively (not only side-by-side).
Manages social “repair” (can recover after small misunderstandings or conflict).

domain.label: Flexibility & Repetitive Behaviors
domain.description: Cognitive rigidity, repetitive/sensory behaviors, intense interests.

questions.text: Becomes very distressed with changes in routine/plans.
Needs things “just so” (order, sameness, exactness).
Repeats phrases or scripts (from shows/past conversations) outside of context.
Repetitive movements (flapping, rocking, pacing, spinning).
Intense special interests that crowd out other activities.
Difficulty shifting from a preferred activity to a new demand (transitions).
Repeats questions even after being answered (reassurance loops).
Gets “stuck” on an idea/topic and can’t let it go easily.

domain.label: Sensory Profile
domain.description: Sensory sensitivity and sensory-seeking patterns that affect regulation and participation.

questions.text: Overreacts to loud or unexpected noises (covers ears, flees, panics).
Overreacts to clothing textures/tags/seams or grooming (haircuts, brushing).
Avoids messy play (paint, sand, glue) or getting hands/face dirty.
Gets overwhelmed by bright lights, visual clutter, or busy environments (stores, parties).
Strongly seeks movement (jumping, spinning, crashing, running indoors).
Seeks deep pressure (tight hugs, weighted blanket, squeezing into small spaces).
Mouths/chews non-food items (clothes, pencils, toys).
Sensory overload leads to shutdown or meltdown.

domain.label: Emotional Regulation & Anxiety
domain.description: Stress reactivity, worry, frustration tolerance, and recovery.

questions.text: Worries before upcoming events or changes.
Seeks reassurance repeatedly (“Are you sure?”, “What if…?”) even after answered.
Has strong distress when corrected or told they made a mistake.
Big reactions to small problems (low frustration tolerance).
Has difficulty calming once upset (takes longer than 15 minutes).
Avoids tasks due to fear of failure or being wrong.

domain.label: Language & Pragmatics
domain.description: Understanding/using language, conversation skills, and breakdown patterns.

questions.text: Understands 2–3 step directions (e.g., “Get shoes, put them by the door, then come here”).
Answers WH-questions (who/what/where/when/why/how) appropriately for their level.
Can tell about their day in a simple sequence (beginning, middle, end).
Uses language to negotiate/compromise (not only protest/request).
Maintains topic and responds to questions (doesn’t frequently derail or ignore).
Misunderstandings in communication often lead to frustration/meltdowns.

domain.label: Executive Function
domain.description: Attention, starting tasks, transitions, working memory, and impulse control.

questions.text: Starts tasks without long delays when asked (with reasonable supports).
Stays with a non-preferred task for a reasonable amount of time for their level.
Transitions successfully with warnings/timers/visual supports.
Gets overwhelmed by multi-step tasks unless broken down.
Impulsivity creates problems (interrupting, grabbing, bolting, unsafe choices).
Accepts “not now” or waiting (delayed gratification) without major escalation.

domain.label: Adaptive Skills (Daily Living)
domain.description: Current independence in self-care and routines.

questions.text: Toileting independence.
Handwashing / basic hygiene routine.
Dressing (including shoes, basic clothing).
Toothbrushing routine.
Sleep routine independence (follows bedtime steps with reasonable support).
Safety awareness (basic danger understanding for age/level).

domain.label: School & Learning
domain.description: Participation, comprehension demands, and common school barriers.

questions.text: Understands teacher directions in a group setting (classroom).
Participates in class without distress (most days).
Homework demands are manageable with reasonable support.
Language comprehension (not math skill) is a major barrier in word problems.
Sensory factors (noise, lights, crowds) affect school success.
Peer interactions at recess/lunch generally go well.

domain.label: Feeding, Sleep & Body
domain.description: Quality-of-life factors that strongly influence regulation and behavior.

questions.text: Has a very limited food repertoire (few 'safe foods').
Gags/refuses foods due to texture/smell (beyond typical pickiness).
GI issues (constipation/diarrhea/reflux) appear to affect mood/behavior.
Takes longer than 30 minutes to fall asleep on most nights.
Wakes up at night frequently (more than 2 nights/week).
Screen time transitions are especially hard (stopping screens causes big distress).

domain.label: Strengths & Preferences
domain.description: What motivates your child and what helps them regulate; crucial for tailoring activities.

questions.text: List your child's top interests (comma-separated).
List your child's biggest strengths (comma-separated).
What most reliably motivates your child right now?
What calms your child fastest when upset?
Which time of day is usually BEST for learning/practice?
Common triggers (free text).
